title: Jeremiah 2: Israel's Two Evils and the Forsaken Fountain
body:
Read the chapter → [Jeremiah 2](/bible/jeremiah/2)

**[Jeremiah 2:1-3](/bible/jeremiah/2#v1)**

> <sup>[1](/bible/jeremiah/2#v1)</sup> Moreover the word of the Lord came to me, saying,
>
> <sup>[2](/bible/jeremiah/2#v2)</sup> Go and cry in the ears of Jerusalem, saying, Thus saith the Lord; I remember thee, the kindness of thy youth, the love of thine espousals, when thou wentest after me in the wilderness, in a land that was not sown.
>
> <sup>[3](/bible/jeremiah/2#v3)</sup> Israel was holiness unto the Lord, and the firstfruits of his increase: all that devour him shall offend; evil shall come upon them, saith the Lord.

- The word comes to cry aloud in the ears of Jerusalem: the Most High remembers the kindness of Israel's youth and her love in the wilderness.
- Israel was holiness unto the Most High and the firstfruits of His increase, and all that devour him shall offend; the nations have devoured us because of our sins.

**[Jeremiah 2:4-6](/bible/jeremiah/2#v4)**

> <sup>[4](/bible/jeremiah/2#v4)</sup> Hear ye the word of the Lord, O house of Jacob, and all the families of the house of Israel:
>
> <sup>[5](/bible/jeremiah/2#v5)</sup> Thus saith the Lord, What iniquity have your fathers found in me, that they are gone far from me, and have walked after vanity, and are become vain?
>
> <sup>[6](/bible/jeremiah/2#v6)</sup> Neither said they, Where is the Lord that brought us up out of the land of Egypt, that led us through the wilderness, through a land of deserts and of pits, through a land of drought, and of the shadow of death, through a land that no man passed through, and where no man dwelt?

- This is the question the Most High is asking the so-called blacks and Hispanics today: what iniquity have your fathers found in Me, that they are gone far from Me, walked after vanity, and become vain.
- They did not ask where is the Most High that brought them up out of Egypt and led them through the wilderness; our people keep doing these same things.

**[Jeremiah 2:7](/bible/jeremiah/2#v7)**

> <sup>[7](/bible/jeremiah/2#v7)</sup> And I brought you into a plentiful country, to eat the fruit thereof and the goodness thereof; but when ye entered, ye defiled my land, and made mine heritage an abomination.

- He brought them into a plentiful country to eat its fruit and goodness, but when they entered they defiled the land and made His heritage an abomination.
- That is Israel: we had it good, and we messed it up.

**[Jeremiah 2:8](/bible/jeremiah/2#v8)**

> <sup>[8](/bible/jeremiah/2#v8)</sup> The priests said not, Where is the Lord? and they that handle the law knew me not: the pastors also transgressed against me, and the prophets prophesied by Baal, and walked after things that do not profit.

- The priests did not ask where is the Most High, they that handle the law knew Him not, and the pastors transgressed against Him.
- The prophets prophesied by Baal and walked after things that do not profit; that is the Christian pastor today, breaking the laws and worshipping Satan.

**[Jeremiah 2:9-11](/bible/jeremiah/2#v9)**

> <sup>[9](/bible/jeremiah/2#v9)</sup> Wherefore I will yet plead with you, saith the Lord, and with your children’s children will I plead.
>
> <sup>[10](/bible/jeremiah/2#v10)</sup> For pass over the isles of Chittim, and see; and send unto Kedar, and consider diligently, and see if there be such a thing.
>
> <sup>[11](/bible/jeremiah/2#v11)</sup> Hath a nation changed their gods, which are yet no gods? but my people have changed their glory for that which doth not profit.

- The Most High will yet plead with Israel and with their children's children; pass over to the isles of Chittim and see whether a nation has changed its gods, which are yet no gods.
- But My people have changed their glory for that which does not profit; the glory is the kingdom rulership, traded away for things that do not profit.

**[Jeremiah 2:12-13](/bible/jeremiah/2#v12)**

> <sup>[12](/bible/jeremiah/2#v12)</sup> Be astonished, O ye heavens, at this, and be horribly afraid, be ye very desolate, saith the Lord.
>
> <sup>[13](/bible/jeremiah/2#v13)</sup> For my people have committed two evils; they have forsaken me the fountain of living waters, and hewed them out cisterns, broken cisterns, that can hold no water.

- The heavens are called to be astonished, for My people have committed two evils.
- They have forsaken the Most High, the fountain of living waters, and hewed themselves broken cisterns that can hold no water, meaning they hold no truth.

**[Jeremiah 2:14-16](/bible/jeremiah/2#v14)**

> <sup>[14](/bible/jeremiah/2#v14)</sup> Is Israel a servant? is he a homeborn slave? why is he spoiled?
>
> <sup>[15](/bible/jeremiah/2#v15)</sup> The young lions roared upon him, and yelled, and they made his land waste: his cities are burned without inhabitant.
>
> <sup>[16](/bible/jeremiah/2#v16)</sup> Also the children of Noph and Tahapanes have broken the crown of thy head.

- Is Israel a servant, is he a homeborn slave, why is he spoiled? That is the question for the so-called blacks, Hispanics, and Native Americans today.
- The young lions roared upon him and made his land waste, and the children of Noph and Tahapanes, the Egyptians, have broken the crown of his head.

**[Jeremiah 2:17-19](/bible/jeremiah/2#v17)**

> <sup>[17](/bible/jeremiah/2#v17)</sup> Hast thou not procured this unto thyself, in that thou hast forsaken the Lord thy God, when he led thee by the way?
>
> <sup>[18](/bible/jeremiah/2#v18)</sup> And now what hast thou to do in the way of Egypt, to drink the waters of Sihor? or what hast thou to do in the way of Assyria, to drink the waters of the river?
>
> <sup>[19](/bible/jeremiah/2#v19)</sup> Thine own wickedness shall correct thee, and thy backslidings shall reprove thee: know therefore and see that it is an evil thing and bitter, that thou hast forsaken the Lord thy God, and that my fear is not in thee, saith the Lord God of hosts.

- Israel procured this unto himself by forsaking the Most High; what has he to do in the way of Egypt to drink the waters of Sihor, or in the way of Assyria to drink the waters of the river.
- Drinking the waters means learning the philosophies and ways of Egypt; thine own wickedness shall correct thee, and thy backslidings shall reprove thee.

**[Jeremiah 2:20-21](/bible/jeremiah/2#v20)**

> <sup>[20](/bible/jeremiah/2#v20)</sup> For of old time I have broken thy yoke, and burst thy bands; and thou saidst, I will not transgress; when upon every high hill and under every green tree thou wanderest, playing the harlot.
>
> <sup>[21](/bible/jeremiah/2#v21)</sup> Yet I had planted thee a noble vine, wholly a right seed: how then art thou turned into the degenerate plant of a strange vine unto me?

- Of old the Most High broke Israel's yoke and burst his bands, yet upon every high hill and under every green tree he wandered, playing the harlot in spiritual idolatry.
- He was planted a noble vine, a right seed, but turned into the degenerate plant of a strange vine: worshipping the white man Jesus and the cobblestone.

**[Jeremiah 2:22-25](/bible/jeremiah/2#v22)**

> <sup>[22](/bible/jeremiah/2#v22)</sup> For though thou wash thee with nitre, and take thee much soap, yet thine iniquity is marked before me, saith the Lord God.
>
> <sup>[23](/bible/jeremiah/2#v23)</sup> How canst thou say, I am not polluted, I have not gone after Baalim? see thy way in the valley, know what thou hast done: thou art a swift dromedary traversing her ways;
>
> <sup>[24](/bible/jeremiah/2#v24)</sup> A wild ass used to the wilderness, that snuffeth up the wind at her pleasure; in her occasion who can turn her away? all they that seek her will not weary themselves; in her month they shall find her.
>
> <sup>[25](/bible/jeremiah/2#v25)</sup> Withhold thy foot from being unshod, and thy throat from thirst: but thou saidst, There is no hope: no; for I have loved strangers, and after them will I go.

- Though washed with nitre and much soap, the iniquity is marked before the Most High; how can Israel say I am not polluted, being a swift dromedary and a wild ass used to the wilderness that snuffs up the wind in her time.
- Israel said there is no hope, for I have loved strangers, and after them will I go; the strangers and the white man, mainly Esau, cannot save us.

**[Jeremiah 2:26-28](/bible/jeremiah/2#v26)**

> <sup>[26](/bible/jeremiah/2#v26)</sup> As the thief is ashamed when he is found, so is the house of Israel ashamed; they, their kings, their princes, and their priests, and their prophets,
>
> <sup>[27](/bible/jeremiah/2#v27)</sup> Saying to a stock, Thou art my father; and to a stone, Thou hast brought me forth: for they have turned their back unto me, and not their face: but in the time of their trouble they will say, Arise, and save us.
>
> <sup>[28](/bible/jeremiah/2#v28)</sup> But where are thy gods that thou hast made thee? let them arise, if they can save thee in the time of thy trouble: for according to the number of thy cities are thy gods, O Judah.

- As a thief is ashamed when found, so is the house of Israel ashamed, their kings, princes, priests, and prophets, saying to a stock thou art my father and to a stone thou hast brought me forth: the wooden cross and the cobblestone.
- They turned their backs and not their faces, but in the time of trouble they say arise and save us; where are the gods they have made, let them arise if they can save.

**[Jeremiah 2:29-32](/bible/jeremiah/2#v29)**

> <sup>[29](/bible/jeremiah/2#v29)</sup> Wherefore will ye plead with me? ye all have transgressed against me, saith the Lord.
>
> <sup>[30](/bible/jeremiah/2#v30)</sup> In vain have I smitten your children; they received no correction: your own sword hath devoured your prophets, like a destroying lion.
>
> <sup>[31](/bible/jeremiah/2#v31)</sup> O generation, see ye the word of the Lord. Have I been a wilderness unto Israel? a land of darkness? wherefore say my people, We are lords; we will come no more unto thee?
>
> <sup>[32](/bible/jeremiah/2#v32)</sup> Can a maid forget her ornaments, or a bride her attire? yet my people have forgotten me days without number.

- The Most High has smitten their children, but they received no correction, and their own sword devoured their prophets like a destroying lion.
- He asks whether He has been a wilderness to Israel; a maid does not forget her ornaments nor a bride her attire, yet My people have forgotten Me days without number.

**[Jeremiah 2:33-35](/bible/jeremiah/2#v33)**

> <sup>[33](/bible/jeremiah/2#v33)</sup> Why trimmest thou thy way to seek love? therefore hast thou also taught the wicked ones thy ways.
>
> <sup>[34](/bible/jeremiah/2#v34)</sup> Also in thy skirts is found the blood of the souls of the poor innocents: I have not found it by secret search, but upon all these.
>
> <sup>[35](/bible/jeremiah/2#v35)</sup> Yet thou sayest, Because I am innocent, surely his anger shall turn from me. Behold, I will plead with thee, because thou sayest, I have not sinned.

- Why do you trim your way to seek love from the nations that hate us, and thereby teach even the wicked ones your ways?
- In thy skirts is found the blood of the souls of the poor innocents, yet thou sayest I am innocent; the Most High will plead against that claim.

**[Jeremiah 2:36-37](/bible/jeremiah/2#v36)**

> <sup>[36](/bible/jeremiah/2#v36)</sup> Why gaddest thou about so much to change thy way? thou also shalt be ashamed of Egypt, as thou wast ashamed of Assyria.
>
> <sup>[37](/bible/jeremiah/2#v37)</sup> Yea, thou shalt go forth from him, and thine hands upon thine head: for the Lord hath rejected thy confidences, and thou shalt not prosper in them.

- Israel gads about so much to change his way, leaning on one nation after another; he shall be ashamed of Egypt as he was ashamed of Assyria.
- Egypt today is spiritual, the white man Esau, and Israel will be ashamed of leaning on the nations, for the Most High has rejected his confidences and he shall not prosper in them.
